thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscaler_gap_high detected in eu-west-1 — queue depth > 12000 for gpu-pool-3. Pager sent to oncall.

alex (oncall): seeing 5xx spike and queue growth on inference gateway — autoscaler reports "scale_limit_reached" and controller stuck in backoff. Customers hitting 503/504.

sara: confirmed, dashboard shows continuous enqueue rate ~210rps, avg latency pushing >2.5s, queue length climbing. autoscaler metrics: desired_replicas=48, current=16, max_configured=16.

jun: who owns the pool config? looks like gpu-pool-3 was pinned to max 16 due to a historical cap. We probably need temporary override.

alex (oncall): paging infra and ops. quick mitigation ideas: 1) bump max for pool 3 2) enable fallback routing to lower-cost model for non-SLA traffic 3) shed low-priority jobs.

ops_pager: @alex oncall acknowledged. Initiating handoff to oncall infra.

infra-bot: Provider: cloud-gpu-eu API returning intermittent 429s; recent events: spot eviction spikes in region eu-west-1 causing capacity flapping. autoscaler backoff counter=7, last_scale_err="provider_rate_limit".

mike: I can do an emergency bump to the pool quota if we have spare region capacity — executing `rctl pool set-max gpu-pool-3 48 --dry-run` then commit if OK.

alex (oncall): do it. Run dry-run then commit. Also set route-based fallback, enable prefix caching TTL to 30s for embeddings.

mike: dry-run output:

```
> rctl pool set-max gpu-pool-3 48 --dry-run
ok: capacity delta possible=32, will require allocating 4 new instances from provider
estimated-provision-time=180s
```

mike: committing now.

(infra-provisioner): provisioning request accepted, request_id=prov-90712, expected_ready ~3m.

luis: routing config change: enabling fallback-route for non-critical tenants -> `route:set fallback-model=babbage-compat if tenant.priority<50` — applying.

jun: also enabling queue shed for batch jobs older than 120s to prioritize realtime. patching drop policy.

alex (oncall): customers: customer-success - can you post a short customer note and flag any paying customers on degraded requests? need a list of top-5 affected tenants.

customer-success: posted in #customer-ops: "We're investigating higher-than-normal error rates for inference in EU. Mitigations in progress. We'll follow up with affected accounts." Also opening support cases for top 3 customers with elevated 5xx.

sara: metrics update: after commit queue still rising for 60s (expected); will watch. autoscaler events show scale_attempt in flight. provider rate-limiting seems to be the gating factor.

alex (oncall): if provisioning fails, fallback plan B is to route eu-west traffic to eu-central instances (cross-region) for critical customers. Are we comfortable with that latency hit?

mike: cross-region warmup ready for 10 critical tenants. Need manual route override — I can flip for emergency.

ops_pager: oncall handoff planned: alex -> luis at +20m if stable.

infra-bot: provisioning completed for 12 extra instances but 2 failed due to ephemeral image pull errors; final available_replicas=28. autoscaler still clamping due to max_configured=28 now.

jun: manually bumped pool limit to 40 to give headroom: `rctl pool set-max gpu-pool-3 40` — confirmed. queue growth plateauing.

sara: good signal: enqueue rate steady, queue depth now trending down from 12k -> 6.2k over 90s, 5xx count down 72% on gateway.

alex (oncall): start writing timeline for postmortem. immediate action items: 1) temporary bump applied and fallback routes enabled 2) customer comms, top customers notified 3) monitoring alert tuned to include provider_rate_limit tag.

mike: follow-up: provider had transient 429 storms tied to rapid spot churn earlier tonight; opened ticket with provider referencing prov-90712 and api-trace.

luis: creating infra RFC for safer soft-limits: propose autoscaler to be allowed to exceed configured pool max by up to 20% for 3 min on detected sustained queue growth, with automatic rollback and billing alert.

alex (oncall): good. add to action items: run a runbook refinement to include cross-region fallback as an automated policy (canary for critical tenants). Also add playbook step for provider-429 backoff mitigation.

customer-success: received list of affected customers from metrics. we're prepping targeted follow-ups with status and ETA.

infra-bot: NOTE: incident-bot closed on-call pager. Marking incident state as "mitigated" but monitoring continues.

alex (oncall): moving to incident debrief. Key Observations: autoscaler respected config hard cap causing inability to respond to sustained surge; provider-side 429s amplified failure window by delaying new instances; no automated cross-region fallback for critical tenants.

jun: immediate postmortem owners: infra (mike) — provider ticket/soft-cap proposal, platform (luis) — autoscaler config change and policy, dexs (sara) — alerting/visibility improvements.

alex (oncall): timeline snippet for postmortem doc (to paste into GH):
```
- t=0 (1749999999): auto-alert triggered — queue > 10k
- t+00:02: oncall triage; autoscaler blocked at max=16, provider rate-limits observed
- t+00:05: emergency increase requested; provisioning started (prov-90712)
- t+00:08: routing fallback enabled for low-priority tenants
- t+00:11: pool max increased to 40; queue begins to drain
- t+00:20: incident mitigated; partial customer impact (elevated latencies and 5xx for ~12 minutes)
```

mike: I will follow up with a provider postmortem link once ticket resolves.

luis: I'll draft the RFC and a small migration plan for automatic cross-region failover for critical tenants.

sara: I'll add a new alert rule: if queue_depth>5k AND provider_rate_limit_count>3 in 5m -> fire high-priority incident and include recommended runbook steps.

alex (oncall): thanks all. We'll convert action items into GH issues and assign owners. leaving thread open for any late updates. :thumbsup:

ops_pager: handoff: alex -> luis scheduled in 18m if no regressions.

customer-success: will post final customer note after postmortem content is ready.

infra-bot: incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
